unmapped_findings: As-cast 0.04Nb steel austenite composition (EPMA/Table 4): Mn 13.03, Al 8.37, Cr 3.97, C 1.33, Nb 0.038, Fe 64.07 wt% (alloy-level, as-cast information relevant to the 0.04Nb alloy).
EPMA shows Nb uniformly dispersed within austenite grains of as-cast 0.04Nb steel, with only sporadic Nb enrichment at grain boundaries.

Nb addition raises the MC (NbC) precipitation temperature from ≈973 K (0 Nb) to 1573 K (0.05 wt% Nb), enabling NbC particles to pin austenite grain boundaries during the δ-ferrite → γ-austenite transformation.
The austenite grain size of 0.04Nb steels is approximately half that of 0.02Nb steels due to precipitation of NbC particles.
No coarsened intergranular κ-carbides were detected in 0.04Nb steel after aging treatment at 723–823 K (which includes the 773 K/3 h state).

The paper notes that for Nb-containing steels aged at temperatures exceeding 773 K, κ-carbide precipitation was the principal strengthening factor (statement may or may not include the 773 K/3 h state; text is ambiguous about the threshold).
